Write the results to an Excel workbook

Source: R/write_excel.R
write_excel.Rd

Writes the results of run_model() to one .xlsx workbook. In the result sheets, each row is a row of G: first the satellite accounts, then the sectors (the economic block ECO). The sheets are:

Usage

write_excel(res, file, run_sheets = TRUE, overwrite = FALSE)

Arguments

res

Object of class lexio_results.

file

Path of the .xlsx file.

run_sheets

If TRUE (default), writes one sheet per run. With many runs (6 accounts give 720 orderings per scenario), FALSE keeps the workbook small; the same tables are in the all_levels.csv files of write_outputs().

overwrite

Allows replacing an existing file.

Value

file, invisibly.

Details

  • about: the model, the scenarios, the orderings, the accounts, the notation and what each sheet holds;

  • runs, levels, goals and states: the tables of summarize_runs() (one row per run, per level of each run, per account of each run and per distinct state);

  • for each scenario <s>:

    • final_<s>: the last level of every ordering, side by side: the goal g and, for each ordering, Gx, d_minus, d_plus and x;

    • Gx_<s>: g, the Gx of each ordering and Gx - g;

    • x_<s>: the base output x0, the output x_star of each ordering and delta_x = x_star - x0;

  • for each run, <s>_<ordering>: every row of G at every priority level, side by side: g, then Gx, d_minus, d_plus and x of level 1 to the last (the table all_levels.csv of write_outputs()).

The rows are identified by row (the account name or the sector code), notation and name. In the notation, xD_j is D_j x, the level of account j, and f'_h is row h of (I - A) x, the net output of sector h, whose goal is the final demand f_h. The column x is empty in the account rows.

Sheet names are limited to 31 characters by Excel; longer names are shortened.

Examples

res <- run_model(system.file("examples", "toy", "model.yml", package = "lexio"), verbose = FALSE)
file <- write_excel(res, tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx"))
